title: Ranh giới dịch vụ và HTTP
requirements: Two independent Catalog/Orders processes communicate through HTTP; Orders owns snapshots and integer-cent totals.
Validate input and bounded payloads, distinguish dependency outage/timeout, use real HTTP integration tests.

title: Hợp đồng API và tương thích phiên bản
requirements: Build an independently runnable Catalog/Orders lesson with GET /v1/products/:id and a different nested-price /v2/products/:id schema; Orders continues consuming v1.
A pure runtime v1-product parser accepts additive unknown response fields but rejects missing/wrong-type/id/price fields; write meaningful unit fixtures first.

Prove compatibility with additive provider fields and rejection of incompatible upstream data over real HTTP with separate provider/consumer processes. Explain that TypeScript alone does not validate network JSON.

title: Dữ liệu thuộc từng dịch vụ
requirements: Use built-in node:sqlite for separate service-owned SQLite files under configurable temporary/data paths; never share a database file between services.
Demonstrate an order surviving Orders restart and retrieval without the Catalog dependency; use real processes and independent temp database paths per test.
Document schema/migration initialization, ownership boundaries and SQLite single-node tradeoffs, without claiming a production deployment.

title: Truyền deadline và hủy yêu cầu
requirements: Go beyond lesson01 single-hop timeout: propagate a bounded end-to-end remaining deadline through Gateway→Orders→Catalog.
Use AbortController and validated deadline metadata; cancel downstream work when the caller disconnects or the budget expires.
Unit-test budget calculations with an injected clock; use real service processes and synchronization/barriers to verify cancellation without brittle sleep-based assertions.

title: Tạo đơn có idempotency
requirements: Implement an Idempotency-Key contract for order creation with persistent service-owned SQLite records and a request fingerprint.
Concurrent identical requests return the same order; a reused key with different input returns409; a completed response can be replayed after restart.
Test real concurrent HTTP requests, conflict cases, input validation and restart recovery; explain failures still requiring recovery rather than asserting exactly-once networking.

title: Retry có giới hạn và backoff
requirements: Implement bounded retry policy with exponential backoff and jitter for transient safe/idempotent operations only, respecting the overall deadline.
Pure policy tests use deterministic RNG/clock; real HTTP tests make an upstream fail twice then succeed and prove exact bounded attempts.
Do not retry arbitrary POST requests blindly; compare safe GET and a request protected by an idempotency contract.

title: Circuit breaker và half-open
requirements: Build an explicit closed/open/half-open state machine around a downstream HTTP dependency; bound the half-open probe count.
Unit-test state/time transitions with an injected clock; integration-test fast failures while open and recovery after a successful probe.
Explain circuit breaker versus timeout/retry and document the scope/limits of per-instance state.

title: Correlation ID và log có cấu trúc
requirements: Propagate a validated correlation/request ID between independent HTTP services, using generated IDs for absent/invalid input.
Emit structured JSON logs without request secrets and demonstrate tracing one request across services.
Test interleaved requests for context isolation and actual propagated HTTP headers/log records; explain logs are not a full distributed tracing system.

title: API gateway và kết quả một phần
requirements: Build a gateway that concurrently aggregates two independently owned downstream resources through HTTP, without database sharing.
Set bounded per-dependency/overall deadlines and specify an explicit partial-result contract versus total failure.
Test healthy, single-dependency failure, total failure and input validation with real separate processes; avoid a gateway that reimplements all business logic.

title: Readiness và graceful shutdown
requirements: Extend beyond basic listener close: implement a draining state that rejects new business requests, reports readiness false, and lets in-flight work finish before a bounded exit.
Use a local lifecycle implementation if root shared helper semantics do not fit; do not modify root helpers.
Unit-test lifecycle transitions and integration-test SIGTERM with synchronized in-flight requests and eventual process exit; distinguish liveness and readiness.

title: Transactional outbox và giao nhận ít nhất một lần
requirements: Use a service-owned SQLite transaction to atomically store a business change and an outbox event.
Deliver events to another service over an explicitly documented HTTP transport with retries and an idempotent consumer; do not claim to implement Kafka or exactly-once delivery.
Test receiver outage, duplicate delivery and producer restart recovery with separate service processes and durable temp files.

title: Saga và hành động bù trừ
requirements: Build a small durable orchestrated saga coordinating simulated Inventory and Payment services over HTTP, without any real payment/network integration.
Document forward and compensating operations, idempotency and explicit recovery from failed compensation.
Test success, payment refusal, compensation and restart recovery using independent processes; do not call local compensation a distributed ACID transaction.

title: Bulkhead và cô lập tải giữa các dependency
requirements: Build an independently runnable gateway and two downstream HTTP services with separate bounded per-dependency concurrency pools; reject excess work promptly with an explicit 503 contract rather than an unbounded queue.

Unit-test admission, idempotent release, configuration validation and release after success, errors and cancellation; acquire capacity before starting downstream work and always release it in finally.

Use real independent processes and synchronization barriers to fill one dependency pool, prove rejected calls never reach that dependency, and prove the other dependency remains usable; verify capacity returns after failure and deadline cancellation. Explain per-instance scope and distinguish bulkheads from circuit breakers and rate limits.

title: Rate limiting bằng token bucket
requirements: Build an independently runnable gateway and downstream service; use a token bucket per validated bounded demonstration client ID, explicit capacity/refill configuration, and HTTP 429 with a positive integer Retry-After when the client exhausts its budget. Reject before forwarding and never present an untrusted demo header as authentication.

Use an injected monotonic clock for deterministic unit tests covering initial burst, refill boundaries, retry delay rounding, invalid configuration and client isolation. Bound client-tracking memory with a documented full-capacity policy; idle expiry may remove only buckets that would already have fully refilled, so eviction cannot reset a depleted client's quota.

Use real independent HTTP processes to prove exact admitted/rejected requests through downstream counters, client isolation, validation and Retry-After responses. Explain per-instance limits, process restart resets, replica multiplication and why rate limiting does not bound concurrent slow requests.

title: CQRS và read model nhất quán cuối cùng
requirements: Build independent Orders command and query/read-model processes with separate service-owned SQLite files. Orders atomically persists business state and durable event records; synchronize a query-optimized order summary over bounded HTTP requests without sharing database files or importing previous lessons.

Apply events and durable deduplication/checkpoint state atomically at the read model; define event IDs, per-order versions and explicit duplicate, conflicting and stale/out-of-order event contracts. Explain an explicit strategy for gaps rather than silently advancing past missing data.

Write meaningful pure policy or in-memory SQLite unit tests first. With real service processes, durable temporary files and synchronization barriers, prove observable stale reads while propagation is paused, eventual convergence, duplicate/version handling and producer/consumer restart recovery without double-counting. Document source-of-truth ownership, freshness metadata, bounded failures and why CQRS neither requires event sourcing nor guarantees immediate read-your-writes.

title: Cache-aside, TTL và chống cache stampede
requirements: Build independently runnable Catalog and cached-reader HTTP processes. Catalog owns source data; the reader uses a bounded in-memory cache with explicit TTL, eviction and stale-data semantics, validates upstream JSON, and has a bounded downstream deadline. Do not share stores or claim cache data is authoritative.

Coalesce concurrent misses for the same key into one bounded upstream load. Bound both cached entries and distinct in-flight loads; reject overload explicitly, release failed loads, and never cache exceptions as successful values. Use an injected clock and deferred promises for deterministic unit tests of exact expiry, eviction, coalescing, failure cleanup and capacity limits.

With real separate HTTP processes and synchronization barriers, prove cache hits avoid upstream work, simultaneous misses cause one upstream call, source changes remain stale only under the documented policy, failed loads can recover, and overload/deadline behavior is bounded. Document per-instance state, restart resets, invalidation tradeoffs and when caching is inappropriate.

title: Job bất đồng bộ lưu bền và HTTP 202
requirements: Build independent job API/owner and worker processes communicating only over HTTP. The API owns a SQLite job database; POST returns202 with Location and Retry-After, a bounded status endpoint distinguishes queued/running/succeeded/failed states, and completed results have an explicit retrieval contract. Use a deterministic local computation rather than external side effects.

Persist admission and transitions; use atomic claims with a bounded lease and a fencing/claim token so an expired worker cannot complete a reclaimed job. Bound job admission and attempts; terminal failures stay inspectable. Test transition, lease-boundary, stale-token and retry policy with an injected clock and in-memory SQLite before implementation.

Use real API and worker processes, separate temporary paths and synchronization barriers to prove asynchronous acceptance/polling, success, terminal failure, competing workers and recovery after a worker dies and its lease expires, including rejection of stale completion. Document at-least-once computation, result retention, wall-clock lease limitations and why202 is not completion.

title: Danh tính dịch vụ, token ký và phân quyền
requirements: Build independent caller and protected-resource HTTP processes demonstrating a small documented compact JWS/JWT profile signed with Ed25519 using node:crypto, never homemade cryptographic primitives. Pin EdDSA, an explicit token type, trusted issuer/audience and an allowlisted public key ID. Require safe-integer iat/nbf/exp seconds with iat<=nbf<=now<exp and exp-iat<=60, zero clock leeway, and an explicit service identity/scope policy. Never trust keys or URLs supplied by a token.

Use only throwaway locally generated demonstration key material, with no credential-store access, cloud identity provider or real secrets. Validate token size/shape, canonical base64url, signature, algorithm/type, key ID, issuer/audience and time claims before authorization. Distinguish missing/invalid authentication401 from valid identity lacking permission403; keep tokens and keys out of logs/errors. Use an injected clock for deterministic boundary and tampering unit tests.

With real separate HTTP processes prove allowed calls, absent/tampered/expired/wrong-audience tokens and denied scopes, plus rejecting unknown keys and algorithm confusion. Include fail-closed configuration checks and document that this is an educational narrow verifier, not a general JWT library, OAuth server or production identity system; bearer replay and transport confidentiality require controls outside this loopback HTTP demo, and production needs TLS and a maintained standards implementation.

title: Metrics HTTP, histogram và cardinality có giới hạn
requirements: Build independently runnable gateway and downstream HTTP processes with per-process request counters, active-request gauges and a classic cumulative duration histogram exposed in documented Prometheus text format. Use Node built-ins only; no monitoring server, package or deployment is required.

Use bounded allowlisted route templates, methods and outcome/status labels; never label by raw URL, resource ID, request ID or client-provided values. Record completion exactly once across response finish/close, include dependency failures and caller disconnects, and exclude or clearly separate scrape traffic. Unit-test injected-clock observations, cumulative buckets including +Inf, count/sum, escaping and idempotent completion.

Use real independent processes to scrape both services over HTTP, compare exact business-request counters, synchronize concurrent work to observe an in-flight gauge, and prove cleanup after error/cancellation and bounded series under varied unknown paths. Explain rates over time, instance restart resets, safe aggregation, histogram approximation and why per-process metrics alone do not constitute an SLO/alerting platform.

title: Strangler Fig và chuyển quyền sở hữu từng bước
requirements: Build independent facade, original legacy application and extracted service processes, with the two providers owning separate SQLite databases. Demonstrate an incremental migration with explicit legacy-only, copy/cutover and extracted-owner phases while the facade preserves one public contract; do not share a database or dual-write business changes.

Define a deterministic, durable migration/ownership policy that prevents new writes during a bounded copy/cutover barrier, drains previously admitted legacy writes before taking the copy snapshot, validates copied data and resumes safely after interruption. After cutover exactly one provider owns writes and reads follow the same owner; routing must not silently fall back to a stale provider after an uncertain write. Unit-test legal/illegal phase transitions, route ownership and interruption recovery policy first.

Use real separate HTTP processes, temporary databases and a synchronized already-in-flight legacy write to prove unchanged public API behavior before/after migration, new writes during cutover rejected explicitly, data preservation, restart recovery and failure of the extracted owner without writes leaking back to legacy. Keep this a small original teaching application, document the facade bottleneck, migration downtime/data-volume limits and rollback requirements after new writes, and distinguish strangler migration from gateway aggregation.

title: Service discovery và cân bằng tải phía client
requirements: Build independent registry, Catalog instance and client HTTP processes. Run two instances from one Catalog entrypoint; the client resolves a logical service through the registry and uses deterministic round-robin across live registrations. Use bounded renewable leases, bounded registry capacity, validated instance IDs and loopback-only demo URLs; never follow caller-supplied arbitrary URLs. At most four manifest entrypoints.

Write deterministic injected-monotonic-clock unit tests first for exact lease expiry, renewal, removal, capacity and round-robin membership changes. Define safe registration ownership so a stale renewal/removal cannot replace or delete a newer incarnation. All HTTP calls have bounded deadlines; no automatic retries of unsafe writes, no unbounded stale registry cache, and explicit 503 when discovery has no usable instances.

Use real independent processes to prove requests reach both instances, deregistration/lease expiry removes an instance, a terminated instance causes a bounded failure, and recovery/membership refresh uses a replacement without routing indefinitely to stale addresses. Use synchronization or bounded observable polling rather than fragile sleeps. Document registry outage and single-point-of-failure tradeoffs; a lease is not proof an instance is healthy, and this local teaching registry is not DNS/Consul/Kubernetes.

title: Optimistic concurrency với ETag và If-Match
requirements: Build an independently runnable resource-owner HTTP service with service-owned SQLite and a separate HTTP client/editor process. GET returns a strong ETag tied to a durable resource version. Two clients read the same version and attempt updates: atomically compare-and-update version and data so exactly one wins and the other receives412 with no lost update; never automatically replay a conflicting mutation.

Document a deliberately narrow conditional-update contract: require exactly one strong version ETag in If-Match for PUT/PATCH, missing precondition428, unsupported/malformed header400 and stale valid version412. Validate input and integer version bounds; failed validation/preconditions never change data/version. Unit-test parsing and atomic store behavior first, including weak/wildcard/list headers and version exhaustion. Explain the narrow header profile rather than claiming full RFC conditional-request support.

With real owner and client processes and temporary SQLite, synchronize two updates against one ETag and assert one success, one412, exactly one version increment and the winning value. Prove retrieval after restart retains value/version, a client can explicitly re-read and revise a later update, and failures/dependency deadlines have explicit contracts. Distinguish optimistic concurrency from idempotency, distributed locks and multi-service transactions.

title: Distributed tracing và quan hệ span qua nhiều dịch vụ
requirements: Build independent Gateway, Orders and Catalog HTTP processes propagating W3C traceparent through each hop. Demonstrate a documented version00 teaching profile: validate header shape, nonzero trace/span IDs and flags, generate fresh context on absent/invalid input, keep the trace ID across hops and generate distinct span IDs with explicit parent relationships. Use node:crypto and AsyncLocalStorage; do not claim to implement an OpenTelemetry SDK/exporter or full W3C version negotiation.

Write meaningful unit tests first with injected IDs/monotonic clock for parsing, parent-child construction, sampled-flag handling and span completion exactly once on finish/close/error. Emit bounded-size structured span records with allowlisted operation names, duration/status/outcome, without request bodies, authorization data or raw query strings. Explain traceparent versus tracestate, local clock durations versus cross-host clock ordering, and privacy/trust limits of caller-provided context.

With real independent processes, prove one request creates a connected parent-child tree across all three services, parallel/interleaved requests never mix contexts, valid inbound context is continued and invalid context creates a fresh trace. Synchronize a slow dependency and demonstrate its duration/error span; prove deadline/disconnect cleanup and exactly-once span completion. Use bounded local observation/log capture, no external collector or runtime dependency. Distinguish this from lesson08 correlation IDs and lesson19 aggregate metrics.

title: Thay đổi schema bằng Expand, Migrate và Contract
requirements: Build an original Catalog service with old/new executable versions and a migration/control entrypoint, using a single Catalog-owned SQLite database. Other business services never read its file. Demonstrate durable expand, resumable bounded backfill/migrate and contract phases for replacing a field while the HTTP business meaning remains stable. Old/new binaries represent versions/replicas of the same data owner, not independently owned services sharing a database.

Choose and document an explicit compatibility/write synchronization mechanism so old-version writes during backfill cannot be lost or leave new fields stale. Bound each backfill batch, commit progress atomically with row changes and safely resume after interruption. Forbid destructive contract while an old version can still write: use a real enforced retirement/admission barrier that drains admitted writes, not merely an unchecked user boolean. After contract old code must fail closed; rollback is supported only within its stated compatibility window. Unit-test phase guards, backfill interruption and concurrent-write preservation first.

Use real separate old/new service processes and HTTP requests with temporary SQLite and barriers to prove compatibility before contract, a concurrent old write survives backfill, interrupted backfill resumes without omissions, early contract is rejected, old writer retirement/drain is enforced, and new code works after contract/restart. Explain SQLite DDL locking, any bounded maintenance window, migration ownership and irreversible cleanup; do not claim production zero downtime or distributed dual-write atomicity.

title: Event sourcing, replay và snapshot có thể dựng lại
requirements: Build independent cart event-owner and reader HTTP processes. The owner stores immutable intent events in its own SQLite append-only stream; the reader obtains events only over bounded HTTP and reconstructs state without sharing the database. Model a small local cart with creation, item additions/removals and checkout, integer quantities and no real payment. The event stream is authoritative; snapshots are optional derived accelerators that can be discarded and rebuilt.

Write pure reducer/command and in-memory SQLite unit tests first for deterministic replay, domain invariants, event schema/version/sequence validation and expected-version appends. Atomically append against the expected stream version so concurrent conflicting commands cannot both commit. Bound carts, events per stream, page/batch sizes and operation deadlines. Define duplicate command handling or an explicit no-blind-retry contract; replay must never execute network/business side effects. Include a validated derived snapshot with fallback to full replay on unusable snapshot and explain its trust/invalidation limits.

Use real independent processes to prove command/history/state contracts, concurrent expected-version conflicts, restart reconstruction and reader reconstruction from paged events. Prove discarding snapshots yields identical state and malformed/out-of-order history is rejected rather than silently applied; document schema evolution/upcasting boundaries, replay cost and when CRUD is simpler. Distinguish event sourcing from lesson11 outbox and lesson15 CQRS; do not claim exactly-once delivery or cross-aggregate transactions.
